Generated: 2026-11-25T14:58:23.271Z

[001/144] Profile: sensitivity=general | commute=car | heating_cooking=gas | indoor_setup=hepa_purifier
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1. [ROUTINE] Recirculate cabin air & bundle car errands into midday dispersion (Low effort, Today · 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Switch vehicle HVAC to recirculate mode on arterial roads to block tailpipe NO₂ and soot.
     - Step 2: Combine school, office, and grocery car trips into a single midday loop when traffic clears.
     - Step 3: Check and replace your vehicle cabin air filter with an activated-carbon filter every 6 months.
     - Health Impact: Maintain baseline cardiovascular & respiratory protection during peak haze. Keep prolonged outdoor exertion within peak afternoon dispersion hours.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts cold-start fuel burn and urban exhaust idling. (-1.8 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Midday boundary-layer mixing dilutes traffic exhaust before evening inversions form.
  2. [ROUTINE] Run kitchen exhaust & lid pots to cut indoor gas NO₂ and PM2.5 (Low effort, Every meal today)
     - Step 1: Switch on the range hood (or crack a kitchen window) 2 minutes before lighting gas burners.
     - Step 2: Cook on rear burners with fitted lids to capture steam, oil aerosols, and NO₂ at the source.
     - Step 3: Leave exhaust running for 10 minutes after turning off the stove to clear residual gases.
     - Health Impact: Prevents indoor NO₂ and ultrafine cooking aerosols from irritating airways. (General adult household).
     - Emission Impact: Lidded cooking cuts LPG/natural gas fuel draw by ~25%. (-0.7 kg CO2e/day, -19% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.
  3. [ROUTINE] Daily respiratory & hydration check for general adult household (Low effort, Morning & evening)
     - Step 1: Watch for throat dryness or eye irritation when PM2.5 exceeds 2× WHO limits.
     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.
     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.
     - Health Impact: Maintain baseline cardiovascular & respiratory protection during peak haze. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -10% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Run HEPA purifier continuously on medium-high in occupied rooms (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Keep bedroom/living doors shut so the HEPA unit cycles room air 4–5× per hour effectively.
     - Step 2: Position the purifier away from corners and curtains for unobstructed 360° intake airflow.
     - Step 3: Vacuum the outer pre-filter mesh weekly to sustain full Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR).
     - Health Impact: Captures >99% of infiltrated PM2.5, soot, and allergens. Maintain clean sleeping-zone air overnight so lungs recover from daytime exposure.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -34% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Pair HEPA filtration with damp-dusting & sealed overnight thresholds (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Wipe surfaces and mop floors with a damp microfiber cloth so settled particles stay captured.
     - Step 2: Check filter-life indicators monthly and replace saturated activated-carbon/HEPA cartridges.
     - Step 3: Drop purifier fan speed to sleep mode at night only after daytime particles have cleared.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for general adult household overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding general adult household from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Swap one short solo car trip for transit, carpool, or errand chaining (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Replace one short trip under 3 km with public transit, walking (when AQI ≤ 100), or carpooling.
     - Step 2: Coordinate school/office drop-offs with a neighbor or household member twice a week.
     - Step 3: Switch off the engine at signals or waits longer than 30 seconds to eliminate curb idling.
     - Health Impact: Lowers cumulative roadside PM2.5 and NO₂ buildup inside the cabin. Protects general adult household.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts cold-engine tailpipe emissions in residential neighborhood streets. (-2.3 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Shift water boiling & reheating from open gas flame to electric kettle/induction (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Use an electric kettle or induction hotplate instead of open gas flames for boiling water and tea.
     - Step 2: Batch-cook lentils, rice, or stews in a pressure cooker to cut total burner runtime in half.
     - Step 3: Avoid indoor incense, scented candles, or mosquito coils during stagnant winter evenings.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for general adult household.
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around general adult household.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Health Impact: Maintain baseline cardiovascular & respiratory protection during peak haze. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -10% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Set split AC/HVAC fan to recirculate with cleaned high-MERV filters (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Ensure fresh-air intake dampers are closed during smog peaks and run fan circulation on medium.
     - Step 2: Rinse or replace split AC mesh filters every 2 weeks during winter haze episodes.
     - Step 3: Consider adding a DIY MERV-13 box-fan filter in the main bedroom for fine PM2.5 capture.
     - Health Impact: Traps coarse dust and reduces outdoor haze infiltration. Maintain clean sleeping-zone air overnight so lungs recover from daytime exposure.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -20% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Seal window-frame drafts & damp-mop bedrooms before bedtime (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Apply foam weatherstripping along loose sliding window tracks to stop cold smog seepage.
     - Step 2: Damp-mop hard floors in the late afternoon instead of dry sweeping.
     - Step 3: Keep bedroom doors closed at night to isolate sleeping air from hallway infiltration.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for general adult household overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding general adult household from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Swap one short solo car trip for transit, carpool, or errand chaining (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Replace one short trip under 3 km with public transit, walking (when AQI ≤ 100), or carpooling.
     - Step 2: Coordinate school/office drop-offs with a neighbor or household member twice a week.
     - Step 3: Switch off the engine at signals or waits longer than 30 seconds to eliminate curb idling.
     - Health Impact: Lowers cumulative roadside PM2.5 and NO₂ buildup inside the cabin. Protects general adult household.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts cold-engine tailpipe emissions in residential neighborhood streets. (-2.3 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Eliminate indoor incense/candles & run heavy electric appliances off-peak (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Skip incense sticks, paraffin candles, and aerosol sprays while outdoor dispersion is weak.
     - Step 2: Use thermal flasks or slow/pressure cookers to retain heat without repeated reheating.
     - Step 3: Keep outdoor yard waste unburnt; compost leaves instead of open burning.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for general adult household.
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around general adult household.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Emission Impact: Maintains low-footprint two-wheeler mobility without acute particulate spikes. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -28% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Midday boundary-layer mixing dilutes traffic exhaust before evening inversions form.
  2. [ROUTINE] Run kitchen exhaust & lid pots to cut indoor gas NO₂ and PM2.5 (Low effort, Every meal today)
     - Step 1: Switch on the range hood (or crack a kitchen window) 2 minutes before lighting gas burners.
     - Step 2: Cook on rear burners with fitted lids to capture steam, oil aerosols, and NO₂ at the source.
     - Step 3: Leave exhaust running for 10 minutes after turning off the stove to clear residual gases.
     - Health Impact: Prevents indoor NO₂ and ultrafine cooking aerosols from irritating airways. (General adult household).
     - Emission Impact: Lidded cooking cuts LPG/natural gas fuel draw by ~25%. (-0.7 kg CO2e/day, -19% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.
  3. [ROUTINE] Daily respiratory & hydration check for general adult household (Low effort, Morning & evening)
     - Step 1: Watch for throat dryness or eye irritation when PM2.5 exceeds 2× WHO limits.
     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.
     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.
     - Health Impact: Maintain baseline cardiovascular & respiratory protection during peak haze. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -10% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Run HEPA purifier continuously on medium-high in occupied rooms (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Keep bedroom/living doors shut so the HEPA unit cycles room air 4–5× per hour effectively.
     - Step 2: Position the purifier away from corners and curtains for unobstructed 360° intake airflow.
     - Step 3: Vacuum the outer pre-filter mesh weekly to sustain full Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR).
     - Health Impact: Captures >99% of infiltrated PM2.5, soot, and allergens. Maintain clean sleeping-zone air overnight so lungs recover from daytime exposure.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -34% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Pair HEPA filtration with damp-dusting & sealed overnight thresholds (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)

     - Step 2: Check filter-life indicators monthly and replace saturated activated-carbon/HEPA cartridges.
     - Step 3: Drop purifier fan speed to sleep mode at night only after daytime particles have cleared.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for general adult household overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1. [ROUTINE] Wear a fitted N95/FFP2 respirator & shift two-wheeler rides off-peak (Low effort, Today · 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Seal a certified N95/FFP2 mask snugly under your helmet before entering congested intersections.
     - Step 2: Choose parallel residential lanes to avoid riding directly behind diesel buses and trucks.
     - Step 3: Wash face and rinse nasal passages with saline after returning from heavy traffic rides.
     - Health Impact: Maintain baseline cardiovascular & respiratory protection during peak haze. Keep prolonged outdoor exertion within peak afternoon dispersion hours.
     - Emission Impact: Maintains low-footprint two-wheeler mobility without acute particulate spikes. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -28% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Midday boundary-layer mixing dilutes traffic exhaust before evening inversions form.
  2. [ROUTINE] Use lids and low-smoke oils on induction/electric cooktops (Low effort, Every meal today)
     - Step 1: Cover pans while boiling or simmering to trap fine lipid droplets at the source.
     - Step 2: Choose high-smoke-point oils and medium heat settings to minimize pan aerosol generation.
     - Step 3: Run brief kitchen exhaust during high-heat searing to clear ultrafine cooking particles.
     - Health Impact: Keeps indoor PM2.5 near background levels with zero combustion NO₂. (General adult household).
     - Emission Impact: Minimizes electric thermal losses during daily meal preparation. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.
  3. [ROUTINE] Daily respiratory & hydration check for general adult household (Low effort, Morning & evening)
     - Step 1: Watch for throat dryness or eye irritation when PM2.5 exceeds 2× WHO limits.
     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.
     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.
     - Health Impact: Maintain baseline cardiovascular & respiratory protection during peak haze. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -10% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Set split AC/HVAC fan to recirculate with cleaned high-MERV filters (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Ensure fresh-air intake dampers are closed during smog peaks and run fan circulation on medium.
     - Step 2: Rinse or replace split AC mesh filters every 2 weeks during winter haze episodes.
     - Step 3: Consider adding a DIY MERV-13 box-fan filter in the main bedroom for fine PM2.5 capture.
     - Health Impact: Traps coarse dust and reduces outdoor haze infiltration. Maintain clean sleeping-zone air overnight so lungs recover from daytime exposure.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -20% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Seal window-frame drafts & damp-mop bedrooms before bedtime (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Apply foam weatherstripping along loose sliding window tracks to stop cold smog seepage.
     - Step 2: Damp-mop hard floors in the late afternoon instead of dry sweeping.
     - Step 3: Keep bedroom doors closed at night to isolate sleeping air from hallway infiltration.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for general adult household overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding general adult household from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Shift high-smog rides to metro/covered transit or carpool (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Use enclosed metro/rail or shared transit on days when US AQI climbs above 150.
     - Step 2: Consolidate market and pharmacy errands into one off-peak daytime loop.
     - Step 3: Keep helmet visors closed and tires properly inflated to minimize rolling fuel burn.
     - Health Impact: Prevents direct inhalation of concentrated tailpipe exhaust at breathing height. Protects general adult household.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces urban two-stroke/four-stroke hydrocarbon emissions during peak jams. (-1.6 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Eliminate indoor incense/candles & run heavy electric appliances off-peak (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Skip incense sticks, paraffin candles, and aerosol sprays while outdoor dispersion is weak.
     - Step 2: Use thermal flasks or slow/pressure cookers to retain heat without repeated reheating.
     - Step 3: Keep outdoor yard waste unburnt; compost leaves instead of open burning.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for general adult household.
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around general adult household.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Step 3: Hang heavy curtains across leaky glass windows at dusk to slow cold-air smog infiltration.
     - Health Impact: Reduces indoor particle resuspension and overnight smog seepage. Maintain clean sleeping-zone air overnight so lungs recover from daytime exposure.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Build a low-cost indoor clean-air zone & track humidity indoors (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Keep one primary bedroom tightly sealed during night inversions for cleaner sleep recovery.

     - Step 3: Avoid drying smoky outdoor-exposed laundry indoors without brief midday venting.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for general adult household overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)

     - Why It Works: Midday boundary-layer mixing dilutes traffic exhaust before evening inversions form.

     - Step 3: Run brief kitchen exhaust during high-heat searing to clear ultrafine cooking particles.

     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.

  2. [ROUTINE] Use lids and low-smoke oils on induction/electric cooktops (Low effort, Every meal today)
     - Step 1: Cover pans while boiling or simmering to trap fine lipid droplets at the source.
     - Step 2: Choose high-smoke-point oils and medium heat settings to minimize pan aerosol generation.
     - Step 3: Run brief kitchen exhaust during high-heat searing to clear ultrafine cooking particles.
     - Health Impact: Keeps indoor PM2.5 near background levels with zero combustion NO₂. (With children).
     - Emission Impact: Minimizes electric thermal losses during daily meal preparation. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.
  3. [ROUTINE] Daily respiratory & hydration check for with children (Low effort, Morning & evening)
     - Step 1: Keep pediatric inhalers/saline sprays ready if coughing follows outdoor play.
     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.
     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.
     - Health Impact: Shield children (higher breathing rate per body weight) from afternoon/evening smog. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Run HEPA purifier continuously on medium-high in occupied rooms (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Keep bedroom/living doors shut so the HEPA unit cycles room air 4–5× per hour effectively.
     - Step 2: Position the purifier away from corners and curtains for unobstructed 360° intake airflow.
     - Step 3: Vacuum the outer pre-filter mesh weekly to sustain full Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR).
     - Health Impact: Captures >99% of infiltrated PM2.5, soot, and allergens. Prioritize children’s study and bedroom air quality with floor-level dust control.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -38% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Pair HEPA filtration with damp-dusting & sealed overnight thresholds (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Wipe surfaces and mop floors with a damp microfiber cloth so settled particles stay captured.
     - Step 2: Check filter-life indicators monthly and replace saturated activated-carbon/HEPA cartridges.
     - Step 3: Drop purifier fan speed to sleep mode at night only after daytime particles have cleared.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for with children overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding with children from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Swap one short solo car trip for transit, carpool, or errand chaining (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Replace one short trip under 3 km with public transit, walking (when AQI ≤ 100), or carpooling.
     - Step 2: Coordinate school/office drop-offs with a neighbor or household member twice a week.
     - Step 3: Switch off the engine at signals or waits longer than 30 seconds to eliminate curb idling.
     - Health Impact: Lowers cumulative roadside PM2.5 and NO₂ buildup inside the cabin. Protects with children.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts cold-engine tailpipe emissions in residential neighborhood streets. (-2.3 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Eliminate indoor incense/candles & run heavy electric appliances off-peak (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Skip incense sticks, paraffin candles, and aerosol sprays while outdoor dispersion is weak.
     - Step 2: Use thermal flasks or slow/pressure cookers to retain heat without repeated reheating.
     - Step 3: Keep outdoor yard waste unburnt; compost leaves instead of open burning.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for with children.
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around with children.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Step 1: Apply foam weatherstripping along loose sliding window tracks to stop cold smog seepage.
     - Step 2: Damp-mop hard floors in the late afternoon instead of dry sweeping.
     - Step 3: Keep bedroom doors closed at night to isolate sleeping air from hallway infiltration.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for with children overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding with children from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Swap one short solo car trip for transit, carpool, or errand chaining (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Replace one short trip under 3 km with public transit, walking (when AQI ≤ 100), or carpooling.
     - Step 2: Coordinate school/office drop-offs with a neighbor or household member twice a week.
     - Step 3: Switch off the engine at signals or waits longer than 30 seconds to eliminate curb idling.
     - Health Impact: Lowers cumulative roadside PM2.5 and NO₂ buildup inside the cabin. Protects with children.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts cold-engine tailpipe emissions in residential neighborhood streets. (-2.3 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Transition cooking/heating tasks toward clean LPG, induction, or solar thermal (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Replace open biomass/coal heating with layered warm clothing, hot-water bottles, or electric heaters.
     - Step 2: Use clean-burning LPG or induction for daily meals instead of smoky solid fuels.
     - Step 3: Coordinate with neighbors to compost dry leaves rather than burning garden waste at dusk.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for with children.
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-2.4 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around with children.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Step 2: Move water boiling, tea, and infant-food warming to a covered electric kettle indoors.
     - Step 3: Keep a wet cloth barrier along exterior door thresholds during evening neighbourhood burning.
     - Health Impact: Sharply reduces carcinogenic wood-smoke PM2.5, PAHs, and carbon monoxide indoors. (With children).
     - Emission Impact: Cuts residential biomass soot and black carbon emissions. (-2.2 kg CO2e/day, -36% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.
  3. [ROUTINE] Daily respiratory & hydration check for with children (Low effort, Morning & evening)
     - Step 1: Keep pediatric inhalers/saline sprays ready if coughing follows outdoor play.
     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.
     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.
     - Health Impact: Shield children (higher breathing rate per body weight) from afternoon/evening smog. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Set split AC/HVAC fan to recirculate with cleaned high-MERV filters (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Ensure fresh-air intake dampers are closed during smog peaks and run fan circulation on medium.
     - Step 2: Rinse or replace split AC mesh filters every 2 weeks during winter haze episodes.
     - Step 3: Consider adding a DIY MERV-13 box-fan filter in the main bedroom for fine PM2.5 capture.
     - Health Impact: Traps coarse dust and reduces outdoor haze infiltration. Prioritize children’s study and bedroom air quality with floor-level dust control.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -24% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Seal window-frame drafts & damp-mop bedrooms before bedtime (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Apply foam weatherstripping along loose sliding window tracks to stop cold smog seepage.
     - Step 2: Damp-mop hard floors in the late afternoon instead of dry sweeping.
     - Step 3: Keep bedroom doors closed at night to isolate sleeping air from hallway infiltration.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for with children overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding with children from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Shift high-smog rides to metro/covered transit or carpool (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Use enclosed metro/rail or shared transit on days when US AQI climbs above 150.
     - Step 2: Consolidate market and pharmacy errands into one off-peak daytime loop.
     - Step 3: Keep helmet visors closed and tires properly inflated to minimize rolling fuel burn.
     - Health Impact: Prevents direct inhalation of concentrated tailpipe exhaust at breathing height. Protects with children.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces urban two-stroke/four-stroke hydrocarbon emissions during peak jams. (-1.6 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Transition cooking/heating tasks toward clean LPG, induction, or solar thermal (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Replace open biomass/coal heating with layered warm clothing, hot-water bottles, or electric heaters.
     - Step 2: Use clean-burning LPG or induction for daily meals instead of smoky solid fuels.
     - Step 3: Coordinate with neighbors to compost dry leaves rather than burning garden waste at dusk.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for with children.
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-2.4 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around with children.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Why It Works: Midday boundary-layer mixing dilutes traffic exhaust before evening inversions form.

     - Step 1: Seal window frames, vents, and door gaps facing nearby wood, coal, or biomass smoke.
     - Step 2: Move water boiling, tea, and infant-food warming to a covered electric kettle indoors.
     - Step 3: Keep a wet cloth barrier along exterior door thresholds during evening neighbourhood burning.
     - Health Impact: Sharply reduces carcinogenic wood-smoke PM2.5, PAHs, and carbon monoxide indoors. (With children).
     - Emission Impact: Cuts residential biomass soot and black carbon emissions. (-2.2 kg CO2e/day, -36% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.

     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.

     - Step 3: Consider adding a DIY MERV-13 box-fan filter in the main bedroom for fine PM2.5 capture.

     - Step 2: Cook on rear burners with fitted lids to capture steam, oil aerosols, and NO₂ at the source.
     - Step 3: Leave exhaust running for 10 minutes after turning off the stove to clear residual gases.
     - Health Impact: Prevents indoor NO₂ and ultrafine cooking aerosols from irritating airways. (With children).
     - Emission Impact: Lidded cooking cuts LPG/natural gas fuel draw by ~25%. (-0.7 kg CO2e/day, -23% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.
  3. [ROUTINE] Daily respiratory & hydration check for with children (Low effort, Morning & evening)
     - Step 1: Keep pediatric inhalers/saline sprays ready if coughing follows outdoor play.
     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.
     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.
     - Health Impact: Shield children (higher breathing rate per body weight) from afternoon/evening smog. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Create a clean-air room using damp-mopping and door draft seals (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Damp-mop hard floors daily instead of dry sweeping or vacuuming without a HEPA bag.
     - Step 2: Place rolled damp towels or silicone sweeps along leaky exterior door thresholds overnight.
     - Step 3: Hang heavy curtains across leaky glass windows at dusk to slow cold-air smog infiltration.
     - Health Impact: Reduces indoor particle resuspension and overnight smog seepage. Prioritize children’s study and bedroom air quality with floor-level dust control.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -20% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Build a low-cost indoor clean-air zone & track humidity indoors (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Keep one primary bedroom tightly sealed during night inversions for cleaner sleep recovery.
     - Step 2: Remove outdoor shoes and dusty jackets at the entryway before walking inside.
     - Step 3: Avoid drying smoky outdoor-exposed laundry indoors without brief midday venting.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for with children overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding with children from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Use enclosed transit on severe smog days while keeping zero-emission habits (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Switch to enclosed metro/transit whenever local US AQI exceeds 150 or visibility drops below 2 km.
     - Step 2: Use shaded, tree-lined corridors that physically intercept coarse road dust.
     - Step 3: Shower or change outer layers after high-haze commutes before sitting in bedrooms.
     - Health Impact: Prevents elevated exercise breathing rates from pulling PM2.5 deep into alveoli. Protects with children.
     - Emission Impact: Maintains near-zero personal transport carbon footprint all week. (-3.6 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Shift water boiling & reheating from open gas flame to electric kettle/induction (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Use an electric kettle or induction hotplate instead of open gas flames for boiling water and tea.
     - Step 2: Batch-cook lentils, rice, or stews in a pressure cooker to cut total burner runtime in half.
     - Step 3: Avoid indoor incense, scented candles, or mosquito coils during stagnant winter evenings.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for with children.
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around with children.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Why It Works: Midday boundary-layer mixing dilutes traffic exhaust before evening inversions form.

     - Step 1: Switch on the range hood (or crack a kitchen window) 2 minutes before lighting gas burners.
     - Step 2: Cook on rear burners with fitted lids to capture steam, oil aerosols, and NO₂ at the source.
     - Step 3: Leave exhaust running for 10 minutes after turning off the stove to clear residual gases.
     - Health Impact: Prevents indoor NO₂ and ultrafine cooking aerosols from irritating airways. (With seniors (65+)).
     - Emission Impact: Lidded cooking cuts LPG/natural gas fuel draw by ~25%. (-0.7 kg CO2e/day, -23% exposure)

     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.

     - Step 3: Hang heavy curtains across leaky glass windows at dusk to slow cold-air smog infiltration.

     - Step 3: Keep a wet cloth barrier along exterior door thresholds during evening neighbourhood burning.
     - Health Impact: Sharply reduces carcinogenic wood-smoke PM2.5, PAHs, and carbon monoxide indoors. (With seniors (65+)).
     - Emission Impact: Cuts residential biomass soot and black carbon emissions. (-2.2 kg CO2e/day, -36% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.
  3. [ROUTINE] Daily respiratory & hydration check for with seniors (65+) (Low effort, Morning & evening)
     - Step 1: Monitor shortness of breath or unusual fatigue on stagnant high-humidity mornings.
     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.
     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.
     - Health Impact: Protect older adults from fine-particulate blood-pressure & cardiac stress. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Run HEPA purifier continuously on medium-high in occupied rooms (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Keep bedroom/living doors shut so the HEPA unit cycles room air 4–5× per hour effectively.
     - Step 2: Position the purifier away from corners and curtains for unobstructed 360° intake airflow.
     - Step 3: Vacuum the outer pre-filter mesh weekly to sustain full Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR).
     - Health Impact: Captures >99% of infiltrated PM2.5, soot, and allergens. Keep bedrooms draft-free and warm without unvented combustion heaters.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -38% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Pair HEPA filtration with damp-dusting & sealed overnight thresholds (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Wipe surfaces and mop floors with a damp microfiber cloth so settled particles stay captured.
     - Step 2: Check filter-life indicators monthly and replace saturated activated-carbon/HEPA cartridges.
     - Step 3: Drop purifier fan speed to sleep mode at night only after daytime particles have cleared.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for with seniors (65+) overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding with seniors (65+) from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Swap one short solo car trip for transit, carpool, or errand chaining (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Replace one short trip under 3 km with public transit, walking (when AQI ≤ 100), or carpooling.
     - Step 2: Coordinate school/office drop-offs with a neighbor or household member twice a week.
     - Step 3: Switch off the engine at signals or waits longer than 30 seconds to eliminate curb idling.
     - Health Impact: Lowers cumulative roadside PM2.5 and NO₂ buildup inside the cabin. Protects with seniors (65+).
     - Emission Impact: Cuts cold-engine tailpipe emissions in residential neighborhood streets. (-2.3 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Transition cooking/heating tasks toward clean LPG, induction, or solar thermal (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Replace open biomass/coal heating with layered warm clothing, hot-water bottles, or electric heaters.
     - Step 2: Use clean-burning LPG or induction for daily meals instead of smoky solid fuels.
     - Step 3: Coordinate with neighbors to compost dry leaves rather than burning garden waste at dusk.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for with seniors (65+).
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-2.4 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around with seniors (65+).
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Health Impact: Protect older adults from fine-particulate blood-pressure & cardiac stress. Shift morning walks to warmer midday hours to avoid cold-air inversion smog.
     - Emission Impact: Displaces solo car travel and reduces per-passenger tailpipe NOₓ. (-2.6 kg CO2e/day, -24% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Midday boundary-layer mixing dilutes traffic exhaust before evening inversions form.
  2. [ROUTINE] Run kitchen exhaust & lid pots to cut indoor gas NO₂ and PM2.5 (Low effort, Every meal today)
     - Step 1: Switch on the range hood (or crack a kitchen window) 2 minutes before lighting gas burners.
     - Step 2: Cook on rear burners with fitted lids to capture steam, oil aerosols, and NO₂ at the source.
     - Step 3: Leave exhaust running for 10 minutes after turning off the stove to clear residual gases.
     - Health Impact: Prevents indoor NO₂ and ultrafine cooking aerosols from irritating airways. (With seniors (65+)).
     - Emission Impact: Lidded cooking cuts LPG/natural gas fuel draw by ~25%. (-0.7 kg CO2e/day, -23% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.
  3. [ROUTINE] Daily respiratory & hydration check for with seniors (65+) (Low effort, Morning & evening)
     - Step 1: Monitor shortness of breath or unusual fatigue on stagnant high-humidity mornings.
     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.
     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.
     - Health Impact: Protect older adults from fine-particulate blood-pressure & cardiac stress. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Set split AC/HVAC fan to recirculate with cleaned high-MERV filters (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Ensure fresh-air intake dampers are closed during smog peaks and run fan circulation on medium.
     - Step 2: Rinse or replace split AC mesh filters every 2 weeks during winter haze episodes.
     - Step 3: Consider adding a DIY MERV-13 box-fan filter in the main bedroom for fine PM2.5 capture.
     - Health Impact: Traps coarse dust and reduces outdoor haze infiltration. Keep bedrooms draft-free and warm without unvented combustion heaters.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -24% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Seal window-frame drafts & damp-mop bedrooms before bedtime (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Apply foam weatherstripping along loose sliding window tracks to stop cold smog seepage.
     - Step 2: Damp-mop hard floors in the late afternoon instead of dry sweeping.
     - Step 3: Keep bedroom doors closed at night to isolate sleeping air from hallway infiltration.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for with seniors (65+) overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding with seniors (65+) from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Pair transit passes with low-traffic greenway last-mile routes (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Walk last-mile segments through parks or side streets at least 100 m off main arterials.
     - Step 2: Shift non-urgent transit trips outside the 08:00–10:00 and 18:00–20:00 rush peaks.
     - Step 3: Encourage car-owning colleagues to join shared metro/bus commutes on smog-alert days.
     - Health Impact: Cuts kerbside diesel particulate exposure while walking to and from stops. Protects with seniors (65+).
     - Emission Impact: Supports high-occupancy transit efficiency and lower neighborhood traffic. (-3.1 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Shift water boiling & reheating from open gas flame to electric kettle/induction (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Use an electric kettle or induction hotplate instead of open gas flames for boiling water and tea.
     - Step 2: Batch-cook lentils, rice, or stews in a pressure cooker to cut total burner runtime in half.
     - Step 3: Avoid indoor incense, scented candles, or mosquito coils during stagnant winter evenings.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for with seniors (65+).
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around with seniors (65+).
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Step 3: Hang heavy curtains across leaky glass windows at dusk to slow cold-air smog infiltration.
     - Health Impact: Reduces indoor particle resuspension and overnight smog seepage. Keep bedrooms draft-free and warm without unvented combustion heaters.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -20% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Build a low-cost indoor clean-air zone & track humidity indoors (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Keep one primary bedroom tightly sealed during night inversions for cleaner sleep recovery.
     - Step 2: Remove outdoor shoes and dusty jackets at the entryway before walking inside.
     - Step 3: Avoid drying smoky outdoor-exposed laundry indoors without brief midday venting.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for with seniors (65+) overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)

     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.

     - Health Impact: Enforce strict PM2.5 and NO₂ thresholds to prevent airway inflammation. Supports airway clearance across the household.
     - Emission Impact: Preventative daily habit with zero added energy footprint. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -16% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Hydrated nasal mucosa traps coarse particles before they reach the lower bronchial tract.
  4. [INDOOR_HACK] Run HEPA purifier continuously on medium-high in occupied rooms (Low effort, Continuous today)
     - Step 1: Keep bedroom/living doors shut so the HEPA unit cycles room air 4–5× per hour effectively.
     - Step 2: Position the purifier away from corners and curtains for unobstructed 360° intake airflow.
     - Step 3: Vacuum the outer pre-filter mesh weekly to sustain full Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR).
     - Health Impact: Captures >99% of infiltrated PM2.5, soot, and allergens. Maintain a dedicated low-PM2.5 sanctuary room with zero indoor smoke or sprays.
     - Emission Impact: Optimizes existing home hardware with minimal extra power draw. (-0.3 kg CO2e/day, -40% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Maintaining slight positive pressure or sealed filtration prevents fine particulates settling indoors.
  5. [INDOOR_HACK] Pair HEPA filtration with damp-dusting & sealed overnight thresholds (Low effort, Late afternoon & night)
     - Step 1: Wipe surfaces and mop floors with a damp microfiber cloth so settled particles stay captured.
     - Step 2: Check filter-life indicators monthly and replace saturated activated-carbon/HEPA cartridges.
     - Step 3: Drop purifier fan speed to sleep mode at night only after daytime particles have cleared.
     - Health Impact: Keeps sleeping zones cleaner for asthma / respiratory overnight.
     - Emission Impact: Zero-emission physical barrier and wet-cleaning method. (-0.2 kg CO2e/day, -17% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Damp wiping binds ultrafine soot rather than kicking settled dust back into breathing height.
  6. [INDOOR_HACK] Timed 15-minute cross-ventilation in your city during 13:00–15:00 (Low effort, 13:00–15:00)
     - Step 1: Open opposite windows briefly during 13:00–15:00 when AQI dips, then re-seal tightly.
     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding asthma / respiratory from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -17% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Swap one short solo car trip for transit, carpool, or errand chaining (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Replace one short trip under 3 km with public transit, walking (when AQI ≤ 100), or carpooling.
     - Step 2: Coordinate school/office drop-offs with a neighbor or household member twice a week.
     - Step 3: Switch off the engine at signals or waits longer than 30 seconds to eliminate curb idling.
     - Health Impact: Lowers cumulative roadside PM2.5 and NO₂ buildup inside the cabin. Protects asthma / respiratory.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts cold-engine tailpipe emissions in residential neighborhood streets. (-2.3 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.
  8. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Shift water boiling & reheating from open gas flame to electric kettle/induction (Medium effort, Daily household swap)
     - Step 1: Use an electric kettle or induction hotplate instead of open gas flames for boiling water and tea.
     - Step 2: Batch-cook lentils, rice, or stews in a pressure cooker to cut total burner runtime in half.
     - Step 3: Avoid indoor incense, scented candles, or mosquito coils during stagnant winter evenings.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for asthma / respiratory.
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.
  9. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Join zero-burning neighborhood waste & shared-errand practices (Habit shift, Weekly community habit)
     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around asthma / respiratory.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Step 2: Wipe window sills with a damp cloth afterward to remove deposited roadside dust.
     - Step 3: Check the 48-hour Forecast Chart before reopening windows in the evening.
     - Health Impact: Flushes indoor CO₂ while shielding asthma / respiratory from morning/night smog.
     - Emission Impact: Reduces mechanical cooling/heating runtime. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -17% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Short midday cross-breezes purge stale indoor air without letting peak-hour haze accumulate.
  7. [SUSTAINABLE_ALTERNATIVE] Swap one short solo car trip for transit, carpool, or errand chaining (Habit shift, Today & this week)
     - Step 1: Replace one short trip under 3 km with public transit, walking (when AQI ≤ 100), or carpooling.
     - Step 2: Coordinate school/office drop-offs with a neighbor or household member twice a week.
     - Step 3: Switch off the engine at signals or waits longer than 30 seconds to eliminate curb idling.

     - Emission Impact: Cuts cold-engine tailpipe emissions in residential neighborhood streets. (-2.3 kg CO2e/day, -14% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Cold catalytic converters emit disproportionately high hydrocarbons during short urban trips.

     - Step 2: Use thermal flasks or slow/pressure cookers to retain heat without repeated reheating.
     - Step 3: Keep outdoor yard waste unburnt; compost leaves instead of open burning.
     - Health Impact: Removes indoor combustion particulates and VOCs for asthma / respiratory.
     - Emission Impact: Lowers household fossil/biomass burn and neighborhood smoke. (-1.1 kg CO2e/day, -18% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Electric heating eliminates direct indoor NO₂, CO, and ultrafine soot release.

     - Step 1: Compost or bag dry leaves and garden trimmings instead of burning them at dusk.
     - Step 2: Consolidate online deliveries and grocery orders into fewer weekly drop-offs.
     - Step 3: Share daily VayuCheck peak-haze alerts with family and nearby schools.
     - Health Impact: Prevents local hyper-local PM2.5 plumes around asthma / respiratory.
     - Emission Impact: Cuts neighborhood black carbon and delivery van idling. (-1.5 kg CO2e/day, -12% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Open biomass burning emits concentrated fine smoke that settles directly into ground-floor homes.

     - Step 3: Run brief kitchen exhaust during high-heat searing to clear ultrafine cooking particles.

     - Step 2: Cook on rear burners with fitted lids to capture steam, oil aerosols, and NO₂ at the source.
     - Step 3: Leave exhaust running for 10 minutes after turning off the stove to clear residual gases.
     - Health Impact: Prevents indoor NO₂ and ultrafine cooking aerosols from irritating airways. (Asthma / respiratory).
     - Emission Impact: Lidded cooking cuts LPG/natural gas fuel draw by ~25%. (-0.7 kg CO2e/day, -25% exposure)

     - Step 2: Rinse eyes and nasal passages with clean water/saline after returning from outdoor commutes.
     - Step 3: Keep indoor humidity balanced (40–55%) and hydrate well to support mucociliary clearance.

     - Emission Impact: Minimizes electric thermal losses during daily meal preparation. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -20% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.

     - Step 1: Cover pans while boiling or simmering to trap fine lipid droplets at the source.

     - Step 3: Run brief kitchen exhaust during high-heat searing to clear ultrafine cooking particles.
     - Health Impact: Keeps indoor PM2.5 near background levels with zero combustion NO₂. (Asthma / respiratory).
     - Emission Impact: Minimizes electric thermal losses during daily meal preparation. (-0.4 kg CO2e/day, -20% exposure)
     - Why It Works: Source capture prevents indoor NO₂ and cooking aerosols from compounding outdoor PM2.5.
